# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve issue with his heart, requiring regular check-ups to monitor its condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences food textures as a real challenge, making eating a difficult task.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences hypotonia, affecting his muscle tone and overall physical strength.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Hypotonia is a common feature in KBG syndrome, affecting muscle tone and overall physical strength.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences frustration easily in crowded or loud spaces, suggesting potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long-sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia), with squint being a possible feature.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long-sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires careful and regular tooth brushing to maintain healthy enamel.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome, emphasizing the importance of proper dental hygiene.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences challenges in school, particularly with reading and writing, and may require additional support.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences frustration easily in crowded or loud spaces, suggesting potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and medication may be appropriate in some circumstances.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia, indicating an abnormality in the hip joint, and appears to be a bit behind his peers in terms of overall development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Regular dental check-ups: The patient needs to brush his teeth carefully and regularly to maintain healthy enamel.
b) Regular hearing reviews: The patient should have regular hearing checks to monitor his hearing status, especially given his sensitivity to loud noises.
c) Ophthalmology review: The patient should undergo regular eye examinations to address potential vision problems, including astigmatism and short- or long-sightedness.
d) Cardiac review: The patient should have regular check-ups to monitor his heart condition, as he has a valve issue.
e) Palate review: The patient should be referred for a palate review if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns.
f) Skeletal review: The patient should undergo X-rays of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull to assess bone age and identify any abnormalities.
g) Feeding assessment: The patient should be evaluated for potential feeding difficulties, as he is very picky about what he eats.
h) Neurological evaluation: The patient should undergo a neurological evaluation to address his hypotonia and overall physical strength.
i) Immunological evaluation: N/A
j) Gastrointestinal evaluation: The patient should be evaluated for potential digestive issues, as he experiences difficulty with food textures.
